All 28 registered stages passed on the frozen production source, but source-pixel review found the selector/range/meter overflowing the card padding. Added geometry checks after their original suite completed; this run is retained as historical and no source-to-final-test identity is asserted. It is not an accepted baseline.
All four 320/390px cases failed the new card-padding bounds assertions. The 320px selector ended at x307.0625 against permitted x288; native range margins also extended the box.
All four normal and wider-font 320/390px/200% cases pass unchanged range/text/control assertions. Sensitivity grid, activation track and native range margins are constrained.
Disabling native DM scroll anchoring alone did not resolve the problem: Linux drift became 650px after 25 reaction-loading statuses collapsed. The one-line fix was not accepted on its own.

All 28 Mac stages passed, but the Linux container reproduced 650px drift in both focused cases. Original label-only disappearance could also let a test finish during loading; completion assertions now wait for both pagination labels and reaction loading to disappear.
Restoring native anchoring while keeping stable captions still drifted 26px/52px; native anchoring was not used as a workaround.

Controlled delayed reaction responses reproduced 650px late drift on Mac too. Reaction loading statuses were forced onto their own line independently of fonts, then released after the history page had settled.
New user-scroll/late-attachment test found a 120px padding expansion missed by the first content-box observer. Observing border boxes corrected that; no anchor bound was relaxed.

Separate ancestor actual workflow timed out waiting for the newest reply row in protected CHANNEL navigation (20s). No failure cause is assumed and its visibility assertion is unchanged. Final exact-head actual workflow must pass; the local lifecycle journeys are distinct coverage.

Linux microphone/card checks passed (87 controls cases), but original DM prepend case again drifted by 26px. Passing local repetitions alone had not resolved this platform-dependent failure; it was not waived.

A held older-page response and narrow 120px/monospace caption reproduced a 26px pending-request movement: ready label height 78px versus loading label 52px. This is a separate observable loading-state shift, not proof that label wrapping alone caused the Linux after-response failure.

One existing design-system unit contract rejected component-scoped CSS in a conversation component (1570/1571 tests passed). Own runner stopped before real-stack stages; moved the rules to shared conversation.css. This rejected run is not an acceptance baseline.
All 9 focused shared design-contract checks pass after moving the styles.
Original 320px DM prepend case and held-response caption-wrap regression pass with the unchanged 2px bounds; earlier caption fix also passed 10 focused repetitions before shared CSS relocation.
